title: rbac-v2: add RBAC v2 policies + audit logging + KMS & region-pinning controls
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers in regulated industries require stronger, auditable access controls plus cryptographic key management and region pinning for data residency. This PR implements RBAC v2 schema and authorization enforcement hooks across the control plane, adds structured audit logging for all control-plane mutating actions, wires in pluggable KMS integrations for key rotation and envelope encryption, and exposes region-pin controls for tenant resources.

What this PR contains (high level):
- RBAC v2: new policy model, service-level role bindings, resource predicates, and evaluation engine. Includes migration path from RBAC v1 and compatibility layer for legacy roles.
- Audit logging: structured JSON audit events emitted to observability backend + optional write-to-audit-log sink with batch support. Events include actor, request_id, resource, action, before/after diffs, and decision result.
- KMS integration: abstract KMS provider interface, AWS KMS & GCP KMS adapters, envelope encryption support for service secrets and tenant keys, and automatic key rotation hooks.
- Region pinning: control-plane config and tenant metadata field allowing pinning of storage and inference region; enforcement in routing decisions and exporter config.
- Docs and tests: end-to-end integration tests for RBAC evaluation, audit log assertions, KMS encryption/decryption roundtrips, and region pinning behavior. Updated security docs with migration steps and operator checklist.

Deployment notes / migration:
- RBAC v2 ships behind feature flag rbac_v2_enabled (default: off). Operators can enable in stages and use compatibility shim to translate v1 bindings. Migration tooling (scripts/cli) included under redwood/tools/rbac-migrate.
- Audit logging can be enabled independently and supports backfilling from historical events.
- KMS adapters require configuration; default behavior falls back to local key material only in dev. Production hosts must configure KMS URI in secrets manager.
- Region pinning is opt-in per-tenant; routing will prefer pinned region and fall back to nearest region if capacity constrained (configurable policy).

Checklist: 
- [x] RBAC v2 core engine and policy schema
- [x] Compatibility shim & migration tool
- [x] Structured audit emitter + sink adapter interface
- [x] AWS/GCP KMS adapters + envelope encryption flow
- [x] Region pin metadata + routing policy hook
- [x] Integration tests and docs

Related: Linear ENG-3142 for policy evaluator design, SEC-98 for audit schema, COM-12 for region pinning requirements.

Notes for reviewers: focus on evaluator correctness, potential performance impacts on auth path, audit log privacy (PII redaction), and KMS lifecycle error handling. This PR is intentionally large; the feature flag and extensive unit/e2e tests aim to make the rollout safe.

review_comments: Michael Chen: Overall looks good. Two concerns: (1) evaluator hot path — what's the expected 99th percentile overhead on auth checks? Please add microbenchmarks and consider inline caches for repeated checks. (2) Migration: how do we roll back if a bad policy blocks automation?

Asha Patel (reply): Added microbenchmarks under redwood/rbac/v2/bench_test.go — median auth check ~45us, p99 ~220us on dev hardware; added LRU cache and instrumentation. For rollback, the migration tool creates backups and we keep compatibility shim enabled by default while rolling out policies; playbook added to docs.
Sofia Ramirez: Audit events need PII redaction. Add hooks to redact email/user metadata by default and make redaction rules configurable.
Asha Patel (reply): Added redaction layer in observability/audit with default rule set; operator can extend via config. Unit tests assert redaction in e2e flows.

Jordan Lee: KMS error handling: ensure decrypt failures don't cause system-wide outages. Consider circuit breaker + fail-open for read-only paths and fail-closed for secret access. Also include monitoring alerts for KMS error rates.

Asha Patel (reply): Implemented circuit breaker around external KMS calls; added metrics + alert rules in observability pack. Added integration tests that simulate KMS timeouts and verify degraded but safe behavior.
ci_comments: CI: integration suite flaked on first run (timeout on kms emulator). Reran and all checks passed.
Security scan: flagged a high-severity finding for plaintext secret in test fixture; removed fixture and replaced with a test fixture generator that uses ephemeral keys.
tests_summary: Added unit tests for policy evaluation, redaction, and KMS adapter mocks; added integration tests that run full control-plane flow with feature flag enabled and assert audit events and region routing behavior.
release_notes: Added RBAC v2 with migration tooling (feature-flag gated). Structured audit logging and pluggable KMS integrations. Tenant region-pinning controls for data residency. Operators: follow migration guide in docs and enable feature flags progressively.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: auth evaluator could add latency or mis-evaluate complex policies. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout, microbenchmarks, cache layer, and gradual migration with compatibility shim. Risk: KMS outages affecting key operations. Mitigation: circuit breaker, retries, and alerting. Risk: accidental PII in audit logs. Mitigation: default redaction + tests and configurable rules.
notes_for_ops: 1) Configure KMS URIs and IAM roles before enabling KMS features. 2) Enable rbac_v2_enabled in a canary environment first. 3) Verify audit sink connectivity and retention. 4) Optionally configure region_pin policy and capacity fallbacks.
